Bug in the legacy-install migration (`migrateLegacyInstall` in packages/cli/src/lib/legacy-migration.ts).

The marker file that makes the migration run only once also gates the bundle install and the wrapper rewrite. If a process that is not the legacy bundle runs first (a dev build, or a fresh nconnect installed alongside), it copies the state and writes the marker but cannot install or rewrite anything. When the updated legacy install runs later, the marker makes it skip everything, so it keeps running from the old directory with its old wrappers forever.

Fix it so that copying state, stopping the daemon and removing the service still happen only once, but the install step (installing the bundle and rewriting the wrappers) is checked on every start and is idempotent. On that later run from the legacy bundle the result must report `installedBundle: true`, the rewritten wrappers in `rewroteWrappers`, and an empty `copied`; the legacy service must not be stopped again. Once there is nothing left to do, the function returns undefined as before.

This is a pnpm monorepo. Run one test file with `cd packages/tests && node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/<file>.test.ts`; do not run the whole suite. packages/cli imports @nconnect/models from its build output, so after changing packages/models run `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p packages/models/tsconfig.json` from the repository root. Dependencies are already installed: never run pnpm, npm or any install command. Do not bump versions or edit CHANGELOG or the site/ folder.
